rationale: First Candidate on the accepted v1 map. It fixes one attributed follower-side responsibility over F-config: after appendEntries truncates a conflicting suffix it resets only the latest configuration to the committed one (raft.go 1516-1531), while the committed configuration, the atomically published latest copy, and the retained log prefix are left as they were. The claim states the required consistency relation; the binding locates the exact truncation site. No violation is asserted: the code path has no guard that relates the reset latest index to the retained log, and what a follower then reports to GetConfiguration, to a RequestVote membership test, or to a following configuration entry is what a later check must observe.

question.question: After appendEntries truncates a conflicting log suffix and resets the latest configuration to the committed one, is the resulting follower configuration state consistent with the log prefix it retains? Specifically, can configurations.latest/latestIndex (and the atomically published r.latestConfiguration that backs Raft.GetConfiguration) end up naming a configuration index that is no longer present in the follower's log, or a configuration that is not the one the retained committed prefix establishes?
question.importance: If a follower resumes with a latest configuration inconsistent with its retained log, then Raft.GetConfiguration reports a configuration the follower cannot justify, and every later membership decision that reads configurations.latest - the inConfiguration/hasVote rejections in requestVote and requestPreVote, the voter count in quorumSize, and the voters counted by checkLeaderLease - is taken on that configuration. A voter-count or membership error can shift which server sets form a quorum, affecting election and commitment safety.
contexts: a follower whose log suffix conflicts with a new leader's entries at an index at or below the follower's latest configuration index, with an uncommitted configuration entry inside the truncated range
a follower whose committed configuration index lies inside the truncated range
event_paths: processRPC -> appendEntries: prevLogTerm matches, a later entry.Index has a different term -> logs.DeleteRange(entry.Index, lastLogIdx) -> setLatestConfiguration(configurations.committed, configurations.committedIndex)
appendEntries -> StoreLogs(newEntries) -> processConfigurationLogEntry for each new entry -> setLastLog(last.Index, last.Term)

supporting_behavior_ids.b-request-vote: The vote handler's candidate-in-configuration and voter checks consume the latest configuration that the truncation path mutates, so they carry the consequence of an inconsistent rollback.
supporting_behavior_ids.b-follower-heartbeat-timeout: The election-abort guard compares latestIndex with committedIndex and tests voter membership against the latest configuration, so an inconsistent latest value changes whether this follower even starts an election.

unknowns: Whether a conflicting entry can legally appear at an index at or below the follower's latestIndex while the committed configuration index is strictly greater than entry.Index (i.e. whether the truncation can delete the entry backing the committed configuration) is not established from the library alone; it depends on the sending leader's log.

Whether the atomically published r.latestConfiguration is ever read by a consumer that acts before the main thread re-derives configuration state is not yet traced for every caller of getLatestConfiguration.
The behavior of a subsequent AppendEntries carrying no configuration entry after such a rollback was not traced for the case where latestIndex == committedIndex before truncation.
question.trigger_rationale: A single read of the truncation branch (raft.go 1516-1531) shows a configuration reset whose guard compares entry.Index only with latestIndex and never with the retained log or the committed configuration index. That is a sourced difference between the mutation and the consistency its consumers need, and it is exercisable in a controlled single-process cluster by forcing a conflicting suffix that contains a configuration entry.

obligation.description: When appendEntries truncates a conflicting log suffix, the configuration state the follower continues to use must remain consistent with the retained log prefix: the latest configuration and its index must correspond to an entry the follower still holds at that index, and the committed configuration must not name an index inside the truncated range. After the rollback the follower must not publish, via Raft.GetConfiguration or via the membership and voter-count checks of requestVote/requestPreVote/quorumSize/checkLeaderLease, a configuration that is neither the committed configuration nor one backed by a retained configuration entry.

scope.description: Follower-side truncation path of appendEntries (raft.go) when a conflict is detected at an index at or below configurations.latestIndex, and the configuration state visible afterwards.
assumptions: The StableStore, LogStore and transport are the injected implementations; the transport delivers AppendEntries to the main thread.
The conflicting AppendEntries is well formed (prevLogTerm matches at PrevLogEntry) so the truncation branch is reached.
excluded: Leader-side configuration append and the stability gate (b-config-change-append).
Whether a legal leader can ever send the conflicting suffix that reaches the strongest sub-case.

pending: A direct check must first establish reachability of the truncation branch with a configuration entry in the truncated range.
The strongest sub-case (conflict below the committed configuration index) is blocked on whether a legal sender can produce it.

grounding.derivation: b-append-entries deletes [entry.Index,lastLogIdx] and then, only when entry.Index <= configurations.latestIndex, calls setLatestConfiguration(configurations.committed, configurations.committedIndex); setLatestConfiguration writes configurations.latest/latestIndex and the atomic r.latestConfiguration copy, and setCommittedConfiguration is not called here. The guard compares entry.Index with latestIndex alone, so the reset is not conditioned on the retained log covering committedIndex or on the reset configuration's entry still existing. F-config's validity_context requires latest to be a configuration backed by a log/snapshot entry; consumers (requestVote membership and voter tests, quorumSize, checkLeaderLease, GetConfiguration) read exactly configurations.latest.
grounding.applicability: Applies to any follower that reaches the conflict branch; the observable consequence depends on whether a configuration entry from a prior term sits inside the truncated suffix and on whether the retained committed configuration index is inside that suffix.
unresolved: Whether the atomically published latest copy can be observed by a non-main-thread consumer in an inconsistent state.
Whether the strongest sub-case is reachable with a legal leader.
alternatives: The reset may be exactly sufficient in practice because the leader that caused the conflict will immediately re-replicate its own configuration entry, restoring latest; this explanation is not established until the follow-up path is observed.

associations.rationale: The truncation branch and its setLatestConfiguration(committed, committedIndex) reset are the site the obligation constrains; setLatestConfiguration shows which configuration fields the reset does and does not change.

bindings.description: appendEntries handler: prevLogTerm validation, conflicting-suffix truncation with the configuration rollback, entry append, and follower commit-index advancement.
